name: MOV_LoadMovie
summary: Opens the media file number id (movie, soundtrack piece or speech file) as a paused media record.
semantics: Media::LoadMovie(notify=1, id, group, task, flags). If a record with this id is already in the media manager's list the caller is completed with 1 at once (flags ignored). Otherwise MediaRecord::create(flags, id): flags == 0 picks defaults by id (1 and 3: no audio, bound to texture 0x42; 2: no audio, texture 0x3d; 800 and 10001: no audio; 810/811: voice volume; 101..999: voice volume, no video), the file is located by number (movie dir '%05d' / speech '%05d.dat' / soundtrack/%05d.mp3 or .wma) and opened paused; the record is put at the list head with the voice or music volume; answers 1, or 0 if the file could not be opened. The answer goes through the SE group's int completion (Script::TaskSlotComplete) inside the call, so the task does not wait. The record is owned by the media manager until MOV_FreeMovie (or shutdown).
x3_src: differs: B219 - a movie file whose picture cannot be decoded makes no record (0) instead of a sound-only record; B217 - files inside catalogues now open
notes: Completion is synchronous: notify -> vm->groups[ownGroup].onDoneInt = TaskSlotComplete -> resultReady=1 before the dispatcher returns. The x3_src world-hash stand answers 0 at once (stand only).

name: MOV_PlayMovie
returns: int 1 when playback ended or was stopped / 0 could not play
summary: Plays the media record id from its start and suspends the task until it ends or is stopped.
semantics: Media::PlayMovie(group, task, id, 0,0,0, -1,-1,-1, 0). The record is looked up; if missing it is created with default flags (as MOV_LoadMovie with flags 0) and looked up again. Seek to 0 and run; failure: the record is destroyed and the caller gets 0 at once (no wait). Success: if another task was waiting on this record it is completed with 1 first; the record gets the Playing flag and remembers the caller; the caller WAITS (state 2; the call site is a savegame return site). It is completed with 1 when: the media ends (unless the record loops), the media fails during playback (record destroyed), MOV_StopMovie / MOV_FreeMovie / P_PrepareInterruption on it, or another MOV_PlayMovie/MOV_PlayMovieFrom/MOV_PlayMovieVoice takes the record over. A movie bound to a texture (MOV_ConnectMovieToTexture or the id defaults) draws its frames into that texture each frame.
x3_src: differs: B217/B219 (media decoding on the audio layer; catalogue files play, picture-less movies make no record)

name: MOV_FreeMovie
summary: Destroys the media record id (stops it, completes its waiting task, frees the media object).
semantics: Media::FreeMovie: the first record with a media object and this id is destroyed: a task waiting on it (MOV_PlayMovie etc.) is completed with 1, the media object is released, the record unlinked and freed. The caller is then completed with 1, or 0 if no such record. Synchronous (completion inside the call).
notes: FL Ghidra calls the helper Media::DeleteMediaById; it is FL's FreeMovie (delete + notify).

name: MOV_StopMovie
summary: Pauses the media record id and completes the task waiting on it; the record stays loaded.
semantics: Media::StopMovie: finds the record; AP clears its Playing flag and pauses it; the task waiting on it is completed with 1 and the record's owner cleared; the caller is completed with 1. No record: the caller gets 0. Synchronous. A later MOV_PlayMovie restarts it from the start (or MOV_PlayMovieFrom at a position).
fl: differs: FL Media::StopMovie (0x004b47a0) only pauses the record and does not clear its Playing flag (x3_src mirrors this under X3_FL); the waiting task and the caller are completed as in AP. The paused FL record stays flagged playing, so a later P_PrepareInterruption pauses it again and calls the completion of its cleared owner (group 0, task 0); whether the per-frame update reports it as ended was not checked

name: MOV_ConnectMovieToTexture
summary: Makes the media record id draw its video frames into the named texture slot texture.
semantics: Media::BindMovieToOwner: finds the record by id, sets its texture-bound flag (4) and stores texture (a named/material texture index). Each frame while it plays, the manager resolves the index (only if 0 <= index < named+material texture count) to the texture surface and decodes the frame into it. Answers 1, or 0 if no record (load it first with MOV_LoadMovie).

name: MOV_PlayMovieFrom
returns: int 1 ended/stopped / 0 could not play (or id < 0)
summary: Plays the media record id from a start time to an end time and suspends the task until it ends or is stopped.
semantics: id >= 0: Media::PlayMovie with start = (startMin*60+startSec)*1000+startMs and end = (endMin*60+endSec)*1000+endMs; an end <= 0 plays to the media end. Otherwise exactly as MOV_PlayMovie (creates the record if missing; 0 at once on failure; else WAITS until end/stop with 1). id < 0: no playback, answers 0 at once; special case: if arg2 == 0x1434abf4 and arg3 == 0x15200245 it first calls the script method 'MovieNotify' of class 0x96 (CallMethodByName, one argument 0x71ab5124) synchronously - a hidden hook.
notes: All seven args are read without an argc check. FL moved the hook into a helper (0x004b58a0, mislabelled Script::DispatchMovCommand in the FL database); same behaviour.

name: MOV_PlayMovieVoice
returns: int 1 cue finished/stopped / 0 no cue or could not play
summary: Plays the speech cue (language, page, textId) from the media record source and suspends the task until the cue ends.
semantics: Voice::PlaySpeechCue: looks the cue up in the loaded voice tables (MOV_LoadVoiceInfo); no cue -> 0 at once. Record source is found or created (default flags by id, e.g. 101..999 speech files); remembers the speech text/language/page; seeks to the cue start, sets the stop at start+length, runs; failure -> record destroyed, 0 at once. Success: a task already waiting on the record is completed with 1; the caller WAITS and is completed with 1 when the cue's end is reached, on MOV_StopMovie/MOV_FreeMovie/P_PrepareInterruption, or when another play takes over the record.
x3_src: differs: B149 (fixed) - a language outside 0..998 answers as no cue (0) instead of reading past the table; B217 - catalogue speech files play
bugs: AP Voice::LookupCue 0x00499710: the script's language indexes the 999-entry table m_languageCueTables without a check; garbage non-zero word is dereferenced as a HashMap (crash). x3_src fixed (bugs_fixed.md B149).

name: MOV_SetRateMovie
summary: Sets a media record's playback rate (rate/100000); a negative id instead answers a constant.
semantics: id >= 0: Media::SetMovieRateById(id, rate): finds the record and, unless its media object has flag 0x20, sets IMediaPosition::put_Rate(rate * 1e-5) (100000 = normal speed); answers 1 on success, 0 if no record or flagged. id == -35: answers rate unchanged (the stock scripts call MOV_SetRateMovie(-35, 2), which is therefore an identity). Any other negative id: answers GetOEMCP() (the Windows OEM code page) - a hidden query.
x3_src: differs: B219 - every id >= 0 answers 0 (no record has a rate on the audio layer); the -35 and other negative paths are kept
notes: Handler address: the shared tail after the switch (case 7 at 0x00499891).

name: MOV_SetVolumeMovie
summary: Sets one media record's volume on the 0..256 scale (256 = 0 dB, 0 = silent).
semantics: Finds the record by id (none -> 0). Media::SetRecordVolume(record, volume): stores the game volume; if the media has no audio -> 0; else hundredths of dB = volume==0 ? -10000 : volume*5000/256 - 5000 (so 1..256 maps to about -50 dB..0 dB); a value outside -10000..0 (volume > 256 or < 0) is refused by DirectSound (answer 0, volume unchanged); answers 1 when set. The master volume applies on top.

name: MOV_LoadVoiceInfo
returns: int 1 parsed / 0 not found or not XML
summary: Loads the voice cue table XML number file (start/length/stream of every spoken text line) into the voice tables.
semantics: Voice::ScriptLoadCueXml(file): path 'addon/' + movie dir format with '%05d' of file (FL: 'addon2/'), extension 'pck' or 'xml' via the catalogues; not found -> 0. The XML is parsed: every <language id=N> (N > 0) gets a page map (created on first use, kept across files), every <page id> below it a text-id map of cues (start ms, length ms, stream id); existing entries are added to. On a parsed document the file number is remembered and the answer is 1; a parse failure answers 0. Tables stay until MOV_FreeVoiceInfo.
fl: differs: reads under addon2/ instead of addon/
x3_src: differs: B147 (fixed) - a language id >= 999 is skipped instead of writing past the 999-entry table
bugs: AP Voice::ParseCueLanguage 0x004993c0: <language id> is only rejected when <= 0; id >= 999 writes a page map pointer past m_languageCueTables[999] (heap corruption from mod data). x3_src fixed (bugs_fixed.md B147).
notes: AP 0x00499480 has no lookup of the loaded-files map before loading: a second call with the same number reparses the file and adds to the tables again; the map only records the number.

name: MOV_FreeVoiceInfo
summary: Frees all loaded voice cue tables (every language).
semantics: Voice::FreeCueTables: for each of the 999 language slots frees every page holder and cue record and the maps, slot = NULL. Answers 0. After it MOV_GetVoice* answer -1 and MOV_PlayMovieVoice answers 0 until MOV_LoadVoiceInfo again. The remembered loaded-file numbers are not cleared.

name: MOV_GetVoiceStart
summary: Returns the start time (ms) of the speech cue of a text line inside its speech file, or -1.
semantics: Voice::LookupCue(language, page, textId) (language table -> page -> text id, keyed textId+1); answers cue start ms, or -1 if any level is missing.
bugs: AP Voice::LookupCue 0x00499710: unchecked language index into the 999-entry table (crash on garbage). Fixed in x3_src (B149).

name: MOV_GetVoiceLength
summary: Returns the length (ms) of the speech cue of a text line, or -1.
semantics: Same lookup as MOV_GetVoiceStart (argument order language, page, textId); answers the cue length ms, or -1. Scripts use it to time subtitles when no speech plays.
bugs: Unchecked language index (AP 0x00499710), fixed in x3_src (B149).

name: MOV_GetVoiceStream
summary: Returns the speech file (media record) number that holds the cue of a text line, or -1.
semantics: Same lookup as MOV_GetVoiceStart; answers the cue's stream id (the media/file number to pass to MOV_PlayMovieVoice as source), or -1.
bugs: Unchecked language index (AP 0x00499710), fixed in x3_src (B149).
